channel.title: Africa Is a Country - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Africa Is a Country (africasacountry.com)

item.title: Slow death by food
item.description: Illegal gold mining is poisoning Ghana’s soil and rivers, seeping into its crops and seafood, and turning the national food system into a long-term public health crisis.

item.title: The arrest protocol on my fridge
item.description: A year after ICE detained Columbia activist Mahmoud Khalil, pro-Palestinian organizers in the United States are living under the threat of arrest, detention, and deportation.

item.title: Who speaks for Iran?
item.description: Between imperial narratives and state propaganda, debates about the war on Iran often erase the diversity of Iranian society and the voices of its marginalized communities.

item.title: Pilgrimage to power
item.description: From John Paul II to Benedict XVI, papal visits to Cameroon have often come when Paul Biya’s government faced political turmoil.

item.title: David Hundeyin may not be a false prophet
item.description: In Nigeria’s media landscape, anti-imperialist commentary captures popular anger without transforming it, turning dissent into spectacle rather than power.

item.title: Where do the borders really lie?
item.description: In Nairobi, migrants face not just national frontiers but invisible barriers in policing, housing, and work.

item.title: A life in struggle
item.description: From the Nigerian Civil War to decades of Marxist organizing and scholarship, Biodun Jeyifo’s life traced a tradition of commitment—one that now passes to a new generation.

item.title: Senegal’s theater of morality
item.description: As debt mounts and police violence on campuses goes unanswered, Senegal’s government is targeting its queer citizens.

item.title: Greater Israel and the new regional order
item.description: Israel’s campaigns in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran are not discrete crises but interconnected fronts in a broader project of regional dominance.

item.title: Who owns the memory of struggle?
item.description: An exhibition in Ibadan recovers Nigeria’s buried history of activism, raising urgent questions about access, erasure, and whether archives can inspire new political action.
